cohort: Women with first and second pregnancies registered between 2004-2018 in the National Medical Birth Register
finding: Previous emergency caesarean section, unplanned CS, vacuum delivery, perineal tear, shoulder dystocia, and neonatal mortality were identified as risk factors for developing fear of childbirth in subsequent pregnancies.
mod_finding: Emergency caesarean section, unplanned CS, and vacuum delivery during the first pregnancy were associated with increased odds of fear of childbirth in the second pregnancy.
